chunks: And al-Shaykh informed me, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and others, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from a man, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Every ghusl is preceded by wudu (ablution), except the ghusl of janābah.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity caused by janābah
key_terms.غُسْلَ: the ritual bath mentioned here as the subject of the ruling
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: ritual ablution performed before prayer and certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Is wudu required before every ghusl, or is ghusl al-janābah an exception?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding ritual purification. It indicates that wudu (ablution) is required before every ghusl except ghusl al-janābah, which stands as an exception in the law of taharah.
